message: ADD COLUMN region NOT NULL on order_backfill has no DEFAULT — will fail at migration time on any populated table.
help: Postgres requires a value for every row in a NOT NULL column. Without DEFAULT, the ALTER TABLE fails at execution time on any table that has existing rows. Either add a DEFAULT (immutable constant — avoid volatile expressions like now() which trigger a table rewrite), or use the three-step expand-contract pattern: ADD COLUMN nullable, backfill in batches, then ALTER COLUMN SET NOT NULL.

lock_impact.held: instant — the statement fails on a populated table
lock_impact.note: the real risk is the migration erroring out, not the lock

message: ADD CONSTRAINT order_backfill_order_fk FOREIGN KEY on order_backfill without NOT VALID requires a full table scan.
help: Postgres validates the FOREIGN KEY against every existing row, holding SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE for the entire scan — that blocks writes on both the referencing and referenced table (reads still OK). On a large pre-existing table the scan runs for minutes. The two-step pattern is non-blocking: add the constraint with NOT VALID (catalog-only, ~millisecond lock), then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a separate migration which uses ShareUpdateExclusiveLock (doesn't block reads or writes).

lock_impact.blocks: writes on both the referencing and referenced table (reads still OK)
lock_impact.note: safe path: ADD ... NOT VALID (instant), then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT (ShareUpdateExclusive — non-blocking)
